title: The Land of the Muskeg
summary: In 1893 H. Somers Somerset and his friend A. Hungerford Pollen set out from Athabasca Landing, north of Edmonton, with two other companions, a guide, hired men, and an Indian hunter, Daukhan, to travel by the Peace River and the Pine River across the Rocky Mountains into northern British Columbia. The book follows the journey with pack-horses and by canoe through swamp and muskeg, the hunting, the long struggle over the mountains with failing horses and short food, and the descent of the rivers to Fort McLeod, Fort George, and Quesnel. Later chapters are a journal kept day by day. Pollen wrote the preface and made most of the sketches; there are also photographs and four maps.
